- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean-reversion adjustment.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility buffer.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust — introduce early warning trigger for downward revision.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean price — apply downward shift of 1–3% relative to recent 18-day average if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If auction supply events are frequent (e.g., >10 events/30d), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope or apply event-weighted smoothing.
